description: The only test for computeAutoMergeEligibility asserts `expect(result).toBeDefined()`, which passes regardless of whether the function returns true, false, or anything else non-undefined — it never checks the actual computed value.

required_findings.justification: `toBeDefined()` only fails if the function returns `undefined`. Since computeAutoMergeEligibility always returns a boolean on every code path, this assertion can never fail no matter how the function's logic is changed or broken — the test provides an illusion of coverage while proving nothing about correctness. A meaningful test would assert the actual boolean value for a specific input.

explanation: A concrete, self-contained weak-assertion case: the test's only assertion is visibly incapable of catching any regression in the function it claims to test, since the function's return type alone (always a defined boolean) makes `toBeDefined()` vacuously true.
